dimensions.assessment: Affects individual and business taxpayers undergoing IRS audits or inquiries involving third-party contacts, as well as IRS personnel.
dimensions.evidence: provides the taxpayer with reasonable opportunity and a period of not less than 45 days... to respond before contact is made with such other persons.

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative notice protections and time extensions for taxpayers during specific tax investigations.
dimensions.evidence: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply specific federal spending, revenue, or broader economic impacts.
Amends section 7602(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 regarding third-party contact rules.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide for specific taxpayer notice when information is sought from third parties.

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to notices provided after a date 12 months following enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to notices provided under section 7602(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 after the date that is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs or savings for the IRS resulting from the modified notice requirements.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill adjusts IRS notice requirements when contacting third parties regarding a taxpayer's tax liability, granting taxpayers specific itemized notices and at least 45 days to respond under certain conditions.
